enums.name: ScaleSizing
enums.docs:
How a window's size follows a change of scale: `Logical` keeps its
logical size, as winit suggests; `Physical` keeps its size in pixels.

enums.name: ResizeDirection
enums.docs: The edge or corner `dragResizeWindow` resizes from.

enums.name: ImePurpose
enums.docs: What an input method is told the text is for.

enums.name: DeviceEvents
enums.docs: When the platform delivers raw device events (`Event.Device`).

enums.name: MouseElementState
enums.docs: Whether a key or button is down.

enums.name: GamepadButton
enums.docs: Positional buttons in the W3C standard gamepad layout; trigger values are analog.

enums.name: GamepadAxis
enums.docs: Stick values in [-1,1], with positive Y pointing down. No application dead zone.

enums.name: KeyCode
enums.docs: A physical key, by its `KeyboardEvent.code` name.

enums.name: NamedKey
enums.docs: A named logical key, by its `KeyboardEvent.key` name.

tagged.name: MouseScrollDelta
tagged.docs:
Lines and rows of text, or pixels. Positive `y` scrolls the content
down the window, as winit reports.

tagged.name: OptionalText
tagged.docs: Text, or none, which is not the same as empty.

tagged.name: OptionalBytes
tagged.docs: Bytes, or none, which is not the same as empty.

tagged.name: CursorRange
tagged.docs: UTF-8 byte offsets of an IME's cursor in its text.

tagged.name: FilePath
tagged.docs:
A path as Unicode when it is; otherwise its exact bytes: a Unix path's,
or a Windows path's UTF-16 code units, little-endian. In a page, a
dropped file's name.

tagged.name: NativeKeyCode
tagged.docs: A platform's code for a physical key winit does not name.

tagged.name: NativeKey
tagged.docs: A platform's code or name for a logical key winit does not name.

tagged.name: KeySupplement
tagged.docs:
What the key would be without modifiers, and the text it types with all
of them, where the platform says.

tagged.name: Modifiers
tagged.docs: The modifiers in effect, and which side of each is held.

tagged.name: DeviceEvent
tagged.docs: A device's raw input, whichever window has focus.

tagged.name: Event
tagged.docs:
What `Window.poll` and `Window.wait` return: the next event, or `None`.
`device_id` is a positive id per input device. Raw device events go to
the focused window, or the first one open when none has focus.

tagged.name: GamepadEvent
tagged.docs: One application-wide queue, independent of window event queues.

interfaces.name: WindowAttributes
interfaces.docs:
What a window opens with; whatever is left unset is the platform's
default. Sizes and positions are logical.

methods.name: open
methods.docs: A new window; one whose `valid` is false when the platform refuses.

methods.name: listen_device_events
methods.docs:
When raw device events come, for every window: by default only while
one of the program's windows has focus.

methods.name: clipboard_text
methods.docs:
The clipboard's text: none when it holds no text, no window is open,
or the platform has no clipboard to read, as a page cannot.

methods.name: set_clipboard_text
methods.docs: Puts text on the clipboard; nothing happens with no window open.

methods.name: clipboard_type_count
methods.docs:
How many types the clipboard holds now; `clipboardType` names each,
best first, as a MIME type. `text/plain` is UTF-8 text and
`text/uri-list` a list of files.

methods.name: clipboard_data
methods.docs:
The clipboard's bytes for a MIME type, or none when it does not hold
it, no window is open, or the platform cannot read it.

methods.name: poll
methods.docs:
The next event, without waiting. It asks the platform for more only
when the window has none queued and has answered none since the
platform was last asked, so draining with polls asks once.

methods.name: wait
methods.docs:
The next event, waiting up to `timeout` seconds for one; a negative
timeout waits as long as it takes.

methods.name: wake
methods.docs:
Wake the current or next wait for application work, from any thread.
Several calls coalesce; no synthetic window event is produced.
False if no event loop is available.

methods.name: coalesce_cursor_moves
methods.docs:
Coalesce cursor moves inside a caller-guaranteed quiet rectangle in
physical pixels (left/top inclusive, right/bottom exclusive). No move
is queued there; only its latest position is retained. Crossing the
rectangle or receiving another window event resumes ordinary delivery.
Empty or non-finite bounds disable coalescing. Raw device events are
unaffected; applications using only window input can disable those.

methods.name: take_cursor_move
methods.docs:
Disable coalescing and take the latest retained CursorMoved, or None.
Call before changing hit geometry or processing application work.
Other window events automatically deliver that position first.

methods.name: close
methods.docs: Close the window; its handle names nothing after.

methods.name: width
methods.docs:
The content's width in physical pixels; `setSize` takes logical
ones, this over `scaleFactor`.

methods.name: x
methods.docs:
Where the window's frame is, in physical pixels; `setPosition`
takes logical ones, this over `scaleFactor`.

methods.name: inner_x
methods.docs: Where the window's content is, without its frame.

methods.name: platform
methods.docs:
The window for a GPU surface: a platform code, and with `raw` the
four integers xgpu's `GpuInstance.surface` takes after it. See
xwindow-core's `raw` for the table.

methods.name: set_size
methods.docs:
The content's size in logical pixels: `width` and `height` over
`scaleFactor`.

methods.name: set_min_size
methods.docs: A size of zero by zero removes the limit.

methods.name: set_position
methods.docs:
Move the window's frame to logical pixels: `x` and `y` over
`scaleFactor`.

methods.name: set_has_shadow
methods.docs:
The system's shadow behind the window, on macOS and, for an
undecorated window, Windows; elsewhere nothing.

methods.name: set_blur_radius
methods.docs:
How far the background behind a transparent window is blurred, 0 for
none: a radius on macOS, where `setBlur` means a radius of 80, and the
platform's blur on or off elsewhere.

methods.name: set_theme
methods.docs: A theme, or none to follow the system's.

methods.name: set_icon
methods.docs: RGBA pixels, `width` by `height`; an empty buffer removes the icon.

methods.name: set_resize_increments
methods.docs: The steps a user resizes the window by; zero by zero removes them.

methods.name: set_exclusive_fullscreen
methods.docs: Fullscreen in a video mode of one of the window's monitors.

methods.name: drag_window
methods.docs:
Move the window with the pointer while a button is held, as from an
undecorated window's title bar; whether the platform started it.

methods.name: show_window_menu
methods.docs: The system's window menu, at a logical position in the window.

methods.name: pre_present_notify
methods.docs:
Call just before presenting a frame. On Wayland the next
`RedrawRequested` then waits for the compositor's frame callback for
that frame, which paces drawing to the display; elsewhere it does
nothing.

methods.name: set_cursor_image
methods.docs:
A cursor of `width` by `height` RGBA pixels, its hot spot at
`hotX`, `hotY`.

methods.name: set_cursor_grab
methods.docs: Whether the platform took the grab.

methods.name: set_cursor_hittest
methods.docs:
Whether pointer input reaches the window rather than passing
through it; whether the platform took the setting.

methods.name: set_cursor_position
methods.docs: Whether the platform moved the cursor.

methods.name: request_activation_token
methods.docs:
A request's serial, which its `ActivationTokenDone` carries; zero
where the platform has no activation tokens.

methods.name: current_monitor
methods.docs: A monitor whose `valid` is false when there is none.

interfaces.name: ClipboardItems
interfaces.docs:
Representations of one thing, by MIME type, which `write` puts on the
clipboard together so that a reader takes the richest it understands:
`text/plain` beside `text/html`, or `image/png` beside `text/plain`.

methods.name: write
methods.docs:
Replaces the clipboard's contents with the items; whether the
platform took them. The handle names nothing after.

interfaces.name: Monitor
interfaces.docs: A display. The same display is the same handle.

methods.name: refresh_rate
methods.docs: Millihertz; zero when the platform does not say.

methods.name: video_mode
methods.docs: A video mode whose `valid` is false past the last.

interfaces.name: VideoMode
interfaces.docs:
A size, depth and refresh rate a monitor can run at, for exclusive
fullscreen. The same mode is the same handle.

methods.name: refresh_rate
methods.docs: Millihertz.

interfaces.name: Gamepad
interfaces.docs: A connection-scoped controller handle; reconnecting invalidates the old handle.

methods.name: available
methods.docs: Whether the platform backend initialized, including when no controllers are connected.

methods.name: error
methods.docs: Why the backend is unavailable, or an empty string.

methods.name: at
methods.docs: A connected controller in enumeration order, or an invalid handle.

methods.name: drain
methods.docs:
Drain whole 32-byte records into reused storage without constructing event objects.
u32 kind, i32 device, u32 control, u32 pressed, f64 value, u64 dropped.
Kinds match GamepadEvent variants. Returns count; a short buffer consumes nothing.

methods.name: vendor_id
methods.docs:
The USB vendor id, such as 0x054c for Sony, or -1 where the platform
does not report it.

methods.name: product_id
methods.docs: The USB product id, or -1 where the platform does not report it.

methods.name: snapshot
methods.docs:
Atomically copy into a reused 176-byte buffer: 17 little-endian f64 button
values, 4 f64 axes, a u32 pressed mask and a u32 change sequence.
False for an invalid handle or short buffer; no bytes are written then.

methods.name: rumble
methods.docs:
Start or replace finite dual-motor rumble; zero duration stops it.
Magnitudes are [0,1], seconds [0,5]. Reports backend acceptance.
